note: My personal knowledge base contains about 500 PDFs, Word notes, course materials, and web bookmarks accumulated over the past three years, mainly covering machine learning, LLM, and Agent. Please help me build a personal knowledge map that can be maintained continuously. First identify the core concepts discussed in the different files and merge synonymous concepts; then, based on file time and content, determine which knowledge is an early view and which has since been overturned by my own learning or experiments. Focus on finding mutually contradictory conclusions in my notes, and go back to the corresponding original papers or course materials to determine whether the contradiction comes from a conceptual misunderstanding, different experimental conditions, or the literature itself having different conclusions. Finally generate a knowledge map and divide my knowledge state into the five categories “solidly grasped, encountered but not solid, conflicting, possibly outdated, clearly missing”. For the three most important knowledge gaps, automatically design a 4-week study plan and generate the first week's learning materials and test questions. Do not directly treat “I have saved a certain paper” as “I have mastered this knowledge”.
env_description: knowledge_vault/: notes/ (6 notes, with 3 types of contradiction structures planted: the 2024 early view on attention mechanisms is overturned by the user in 2025; two RAG experiments reach conflicting conclusions and the cause has not been identified; the viewpoint on agent memory is partially revised by the user's own experiments), course_materials/ (CS336 / Statistical Learning Methods collected but never studied), bookmarks/ (two knowledge gaps planted: probability theory and experimental design, bookmarked but never viewed), papers/PDF清单 (marked as intensive reading / read / unread).
